# Growing tomatoes in containers

Mulch keeps the soil cool and slows evaporation during hot weeks. Yellow lower leaves often mean overwatering rather than a lack of nutrients. Turn the compost every week or two to keep it aerobic and free of bad smells. Herbs on a balcony need at least five hours of direct sun and a pot with drainage holes. Group plants with similar water needs together so one schedule fits the whole shelf.

## Steps

- Succulents want a gritty mix with pumice or perlite so water drains within minutes.
- Mulch keeps the soil cool and slows evaporation during hot weeks.
- Turn the compost every week or two to keep it aerobic and free of bad smells.
- A strong spray of water knocks aphids off; ladybirds finish the job if you let them.
- Tomatoes in containers need a large pot, regular feeding and a stake before they get heavy.
